relevance_note: The paper describes two children with “TNFAIP3 (A20 haploinsufficiency) variants (n = 2)” and gives individual-level detail for both in Table 3 (P22/G1, P23/G1).
method_note: Read the paper once; no script transcribed it. Table 3 (patients as rows) was transcribed by hand into a scratch file and checked cell by cell against the markdown. Table 3 has no stacked (' / ') cells; the ' / ' in the paper occurs only inside single values ('leukopenia/neutropenia'), which is not a stack. In scope: only the two patients whose Table 3 gene cell is TNFAIP3 (P22/G1, P23/G1). All other Table 3 rows carry other genes (TTC7A, MYO5B, XIAP, CYBB, MEFV, MCM10, FOXP3, IL10RB, IL10RA, IRGM) and get no rows; 36 is the stated cohort size. Also included is the relative named inside P23/G1's cell, 'Sibling died from EBV-HLH' (scope: relative described in relation to an in-scope person); the 'Sibling with Crohn’s disease' of P08/G1 is a relative of an out-of-scope patient and gets no row. No variant description is printed for either TNFAIP3 patient; Supplementary Table S2 (Genetic Variants Identified by Next-Generation Sequencing) is cited but is not part of the markdown, so both variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported' and no variant-level fields are filled. The discussion sentence about 'patients with TNFAIP3 (A20 haploinsufficiency) variants (n = 2)' names that group explicitly, so dermatitis and growth failure (P22/G1) and oral ulcers (P23/G1), absent from their own table cells, are recorded as observed with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. Tables 1, 2 and 4 give only unnamed counts and are not used for individuals. 'P22/G1' and 'P23/G1' are copied verbatim from the ID column; the table notes define G1 as 'Monogenic findings', not a family, so family_label_in_paper is 'not reported'. Two mappings to checklist names are mine, not the paper's wording: 'persistent fever' to 'recurrent fever', and 'dermatitis' to 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)'. 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' is left 'not reported' for both patients, because the paper states no ulcer or intestinal inflammation for them individually (only the CD and IBDU disease labels). No contradictions were found. is_proband=false is supported by the Table 3 row (the paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case'); for cites_prior_report_of_same_patients=false no supporting quote exists, so its span is null.
